newsitem.title: USA: Court says KLM case vs Northwest Air to proceed.
newsitem.headline: Court says KLM case vs Northwest Air to proceed.

text.p: A Delaware Chancery Court Wednesday rejected a request from Northwest Airlines Corp to dismiss a lawsuit filed by KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV challenging Northwest's shareholder rights plan, adopted in 1995.

"Today's procedural ruling does not address or affect the substance of KLM's lawsuit, which is wholly without merit," Northwest senior vice president and general counsel Doug Steenland said in a statement.

Northwest said it filed a procedural motion in February 1996 suggesting that KLM's complaint was premature and should be litigated, if at all, closer to an option exercise date in August 1998. The court ruled that the case should proceed.
"Northwest will continue to vigorously defend its actions in this case and we have every expectation that the court will rule in our favor on our merits," Steenland added.
KLM officials could not be reached for comment.
The ruling is the latest skirmish in a battle between the two companies over KLM's influence on the once-struggling U.S. carrier.
KLM bought a 20 percent stake in Northwest in 1989 for $400 million. In December 1995 it filed a lawsuit seeking to remove a newly enacted shareholder rights plan.

The rights plan makes responses to friendly takeover proposals easier by removing some of the power granted to KLM as a condition of its participation in the 1989 buyout and a 1993 deal that resulted in $870 million in labor savings.
